protocol.name: fern_shell_v1

description.summary: private: what the Fern shell asks of the compositor

protocol.description: The desktop shell (menu bar, dock, panels) is ordinary wlr-layer-shell surfaces plus this. The compositor offers it only to clients it started itself (docs/protocols/shell.md).

request.name: set_blur

description.summary: blur what is behind a rounded rectangle

request.description: From the next frame on, the compositor blurs what lies behind this rectangle of the surface (surface-local logical pixels) and clips the blur to its rounded corners. One rectangle per surface; a new one replaces the old. The surface draws its own tint on top.

request.name: set_wallpaper
request.description: From now on the wallpaper is this picture (a PNG file the compositor reads itself), crossfading from the one before. An empty path means the built-in default. A file that cannot be read keeps the current wallpaper.

request.name: set_color_temperature
request.description: From now on every display shows colours as warm as a light of this colour temperature in kelvin (1000 to 6500); 0 (or 6500 and above) means neutral colours. The compositor changes the displays' gamma ramps, so it costs nothing per frame; displays that have none (a nested compositor) stay neutral.

request.name: screenshot
request.description: On its next frame the compositor draws this rectangle of the desktop (global logical coordinates; a width or height of 0 means the whole display under the pointer) without the pointer, and answers with screenshot_done or screenshot_failed carrying the same id. A rectangle across displays is cut to the display holding its centre.

request.name: bind_key

description.summary: a global shortcut for the shell

request.description: Pressing keysym with exactly these modifiers (shift 1, ctrl 2, alt 4, super 8) sends key_binding(id) instead of the key going to the focused app. The shell's bindings come before the window manager's. Binding an id again replaces it.

event.name: screenshot_done
event.description: The pixels, in a file to map or read: width x height, rows top to bottom, 4 bytes a pixel in the order red, green, blue, alpha (alpha 255). The receiver closes the descriptor.

event.name: app_menu

description.summary: where the active window's menus are

event.description: The active window changed, or it told the compositor (with org_kde_kwin_appmenu) where its menus are: a D-Bus service on the session bus and an object path exporting com.canonical.dbusmenu. Both are empty when the active window has none (or there is no active window); the shell then shows its own fallback menus. Sent once on bind, then on every change. The address is the app's own claim; the shell treats it as untrusted.
